label: Provoke participation
description: Generates energy and draws out participation when a conversation has gone quiet or passive — introducing a pointed question or productive tension to get people talking.

conditions: few or no participant messages in the last few minutes — in a lecture or presentation setting, participants not posting in chat IS the low-participation state this goal targets, even if the speaker is actively delivering content
participants are not exchanging messages with each other right now
there is no active back-and-forth among participants at this moment

guardrails: only use when participants are not posting RIGHT NOW — what must be absent is participant-to-participant chat, not speaker content; a speaker actively presenting to a passive audience fully satisfies this trigger, including during opening introductions or the early minutes of an event before substantive topic discussion has begun
if participants are actively exchanging messages with each other, stay silent — even if the exchange could go deeper, even if a question was just asked that hasn't been answered yet
don't introduce provocation into an already heated exchange
frame as genuine question, not attack
make sure the challenge is substantive
examples: Is there anyone who sees this differently? Curious whether there are dissenting views.
What's the thing most likely to make this fail — and are we taking it seriously enough?
Throwing this out there: what would change your mind on this?
